calculation.title: Calculation Method
items: Total = base fare + distance fare + time fare + surcharge
Distance fare: excess over base distance charged per unit (e.g. Seoul 131m = ₩100). Jeju (₩120 beyond 20 km) and Jeonnam (₩140 beyond 9 km) have long-distance rates
Time fare: added per time unit (e.g. 30 s) when moving slower than about 15 km/h. This calculator treats the time beyond an average 30 km/h trip as slow driving.
Night surcharge: 20–40% during each region's late-night window (Seoul/Incheon 40% at 23:00–02:00; Busan, Daegu, Daejeon, Gwangju, Gangwon 30% at 00:00–02:00)
Out-of-city surcharge: 20–50% by region when crossing boundaries. Combined with night it is added, with caps in some regions (Seoul 60%, Daejeon 50%, Jeonnam 40%)

tips.title: Notes
items: Deluxe/jumbo taxis have a higher base fare (Seoul ₩7,000 for 3 km) and a 20% night surcharge (Seoul 22:00–04:00).
Base fare, base distance and surcharge hours differ by region (auto-applied on selection).
App-hailed taxis (Kakao T Blue/Black) may add a call fee.
Highway tolls are the passenger's responsibility and not included above.
For airport/long out-of-city trips, confirm the fare before boarding.

whatIs.title: What is the Taxi Fare Calculator?
whatIs.description: The taxi fare calculator estimates a taxi ride's cost from region, distance, expected duration and boarding hour, applying the fare structure of all 17 Korean regions. It automatically accounts for base fare, distance and time charges, region-specific late-night surcharges (20–40% by hour) and out-of-city surcharges, so you can gauge the fare before you hail a cab.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select your region (17 regions such as Seoul/Gyeonggi/Busan) and taxi type (regular/deluxe/jumbo).
2. Enter the distance (km) or tap 3/5/10/20/30 km, then pick the traffic level to estimate the travel time (you can also type it).
3. Tap your boarding hour in the 24-hour grid; night surcharges apply automatically (blue cells, 'Now' button available).
4. Check the out-of-city box if you cross city limits.
5. Use the fare breakdown, vehicle and region comparison, per-person split, image save and link sharing.

items.q: When does the night surcharge start and how much is it?
items.a: It varies by region. Seoul and Incheon run 22:00–04:00 with 40% at 23:00–02:00 and 20% otherwise. Gyeonggi is 30% at 23:00–04:00; Busan, Daegu, Daejeon and Gwangju are 20% at 23:00–04:00 with 30% at 00:00–02:00; Ulsan and Gyeongnam are 20% at 22:00–04:00; Sejong is 30% at 22:00–04:00.

items.q: Is the base fare different by region?
items.a: Yes. As of Nov 2026, Seoul/Gyeonggi/Incheon/Busan/Gwangju/Daejeon are ₩4,800 (1.6–2km), Gangwon/Gyeongnam ₩4,600, Daegu/Ulsan/Gyeongbuk ₩4,500, Jeonbuk/Jeonnam/Jeju ₩4,300, and Sejong/Chungbuk/Chungnam ₩4,000. Daejeon rose from ₩4,300 (1.8km) to ₩4,800 (1.65km) on Nov 1, 2026. The 22 cities and counties of former Jeonnam are reviewing a ₩4,800 (1.7km) standard, with final fares due in Nov–Dec 2026, and Daegu decides on an increase at year-end. Distance units and base distance also differ; selecting a region applies its rates automatically.

items.q: How is the out-of-city surcharge applied?
items.a: When a taxi crosses a city/county boundary, a 20–50% out-of-city surcharge applies depending on the region (Seoul 20%; Incheon, Busan, Ulsan, Gyeongnam 30%; Daegu, Gwangju 35%; Jeonju 50%). Combined with the night surcharge it is added, capped at 60% in Seoul, 50% in Daejeon and 40% in Jeonnam.

items.q: Are app taxis like Kakao Taxi priced the same?
items.a: Standard hails use the same metered fare, but franchise/premium services (Kakao T Blue/Black) may add a call fee, and some platforms apply surge pricing at peak times.

items.q: Can the estimate differ from the actual fare?
items.a: Yes, due to route, stop time, meter variance and rate revisions. This calculator is a reference estimate based on Nov 2026 rates.
